summary: Regression testing after code review refactors (top-level `import json` in server.py, useCallback wrappers across 11 pages). Refactors verified — no behaviour changes. 5/6 backend regression tests pass; all frontend pages load & refetch correctly with NO infinite loops. One PRE-EXISTING backend bug found in /api/account/export unrelated to the refactor.

critical.issue: Returns 500 due to `KeyError: 'id'` at server.py:962 — `brand_doc['id']` when brand_doc doc has only `_id` (ObjectId), not a normalized string `id`. The `json.dumps` refactor itself is CORRECT — the crash happens on line 962, BEFORE the json.dumps call on line 998, so this is a pre-existing data-shape bug (not caused by the refactor). Also affects line 964 (orders_as_seller).
critical.fix_hint: Use `brand_doc.get('id') or str(brand_doc['_id'])` (and same for line 964), OR normalize brand_doc via existing `_serialise_doc`/id helper before use.

context_for_next_testing_agent: The 11-page useCallback refactor is confirmed regression-safe (no infinite loops on any page). Backend `import json` refactor works. Only outstanding issue: /api/account/export KeyError on brand_doc['id'] (pre-existing data-shape bug at server.py:962/964, not from this refactor).
rca of the issue: Endpoint code at server.py:962 does `products = await db.products.find({'brand_id': brand_doc['id']}).to_list(1000) if brand_doc else []`. For the demo user, `brand_doc` exists (they have brand role) but the raw Motor document only has `_id`, not a string `id` key — hence KeyError. The subsequent json.dumps line (998) is never reached, proving the refactor itself is fine. Fix: replace `brand_doc['id']` with `str(brand_doc.get('id') or brand_doc['_id'])` on lines 962 and 964, or serialize brand_doc first.
